sources.name: Maryland General Assembly · Transportation §21-810
sources.notes: 12–15 mph over $60; 16–19 $80; 20–29 $140; 30–39 $270; 40+ $500. Double these amounts when workers are present. This is not the schedule for other Maryland camera programs.

sources.name: Virginia Legislative Information System · §46.2-882.1
sources.notes: At least 10 mph over; civil penalty shall not exceed $100. Work-zone liability requires workers present. A personally issued summons can carry different record consequences from a mailed notice. Page includes future 2027 provisions; those are not applied.

sources.name: Virginia Legislative Information System · §46.2-878.3
sources.notes: Where prepayment is permitted: $6 per mph ordinary, $7 for specified school/work-zone offenses. Extra $100 for over 80 but below 86 on a 65 mph road. Other specified residential rules not modeled.

sources.name: Virginia Legislative Information System · §46.2-862
sources.notes: Reckless-driving speed threshold: 20 mph or more above the limit, or over 85 mph regardless of limit.

sources.name: California Legislature · Vehicle Code §22426
sources.notes: AB 645 pilot: 11–15 mph over $50; 16–25 $100; 26+ $200 unless actual speed is at least 100 mph, then $500. Civil penalty, no violation point.

sources.name: California Legislature · Vehicle Code §22425
sources.notes: Six designated local jurisdictions only. Excludes interstates, state routes and other specified roads. Initial 60-day warning periods; vehicle’s first 11–15 mph violation in a jurisdiction is a warning. Income-based reductions available.

sources.name: New Jersey Courts · Published Statewide Violations Bureau Schedule
sources.notes: Document is dated July 29, 2021. Retained as a dated source; not enabled for a current monetary calculation until superseding schedules and applicability are checked.

sources.name: New Jersey DOT · Red Light Running Pilot
sources.notes: Agency reports that the former red-light pilot ended December 16, 2014. Historical camera lists do not establish present enforcement authority.

sources.name: DC Office of Documents · 18 DCMR §2600
sources.notes: Current index lists an August 7, 2026 amendment. The adopted text was subsequently retrieved and verified as source dc-adopted; the earlier calculation hold has been resolved.

sources.name: Maine Legislature · 29-A §2074
sources.notes: §2074(3-A): Maine Turnpike/interstate speeding under 30 mph over carries a statutory minimum $50. This is a floor, not the court fine schedule or an exact payable amount. 30+ mph over is a criminal matter under subsection 3.

sources.name: Maine Legislature · 29-A §2117
sources.notes: Restricts state/municipal camera proof or enforcement of Title 29-A; statutory exceptions include school-bus and Turnpike toll enforcement. Those exceptions are not general speed-camera authority.

sources.name: New Hampshire General Court · RSA 265:60
sources.notes: Paragraph V standard tiers: $50/$75/$100/$200/$350. Paragraph VI has separate 65 mph and 70 mph road tiers. The statute explicitly adds a penalty assessment; these are not payable totals.

sources.name: New Hampshire General Court · RSA 236:130
sources.notes: Highway-surveillance prohibition contains exceptions and provisions effective September 17, 2026. This review does not turn all roadside cameras into violation-enforcement cameras or claim a universal camera ban.

sources.name: Massachusetts Legislature · Chapter 90 §20
sources.notes: Speeding minimum $50 plus $10 per mph exceeding 10 mph over. Separately provides a $50 speeding surcharge and a $5 motor-vehicle surcharge; these are explicitly excluded from the displayed base minimum. Commercial-load and license consequences differ.

sources.name: Rhode Island Legislature · §31-41.1-4
sources.notes: First-offense schedule lists $95 for 1–10 mph over and a $205 minimum at 11 mph over, with $10 per additional mph. Additional judicial/repeat consequences are not folded into a fixed ticket total; technology surcharge is separate.

sources.name: Rhode Island Legislature · §31-41.3-15
sources.notes: School-zone camera penalty $50 per offense; new-system first 30 days require warnings. Not a moving violation for driving-record purposes. This review models the penalty for an established qualifying program violation, not all program operating conditions.

sources.name: Connecticut General Assembly · §§14-307b–14-307c
sources.notes: Municipal speed-camera violations require 10+ mph over, local ordinance and DOT-approved locations. Caps are $50 first/$75 subsequent within one year; a separate electronic-processing fee may be up to $15. First 30 days at a new location require warnings.

sources.name: Connecticut General Assembly · §13a-263
sources.notes: 10+ mph over in an operational work zone: first written warning; second/subsequent within one year $75. At 85 mph or more the fine is $75 even for a first offense. An officer citation for the same violation changes owner liability.

sources.name: Connecticut DOT · Current Know the Zone FAQ
sources.notes: 2026 program restarted with warnings through July 5 and citations from July 6. Work-zone posted limits must be 45 mph or greater; current FAQ corroborates §13a-263 first warning/$75 subsequent and 85 mph rule.

sources.name: Connecticut General Assembly · 2026 Supplement §14-219
sources.notes: §14-219(c): ordinary passenger-vehicle speeding over 70 through 85 mph on multi-lane limited-access highways, or over 60 through 85 on other highways, carries $100–$150. Lower speeds, trucks, younger drivers, special zones and reckless-driving charges require separate assessment.

sources.name: Delaware General Assembly · 21 Del.C. §4169(c)
sources.notes: First base $20/subsequent within 24 months $25. Add per mph over: 6–15: $1/$2; 16–19: $2/$3; 20+: $3/$4. Paragraph (4) specifically says second offense for the higher repeat rate; this calculator withholds third+ scenarios.

sources.name: Delaware General Assembly · 21 Del.C. §4170A
sources.notes: Authorized work-zone and specified residence-district systems, 11+ mph over. Civil penalty follows §4169(c). Work-zone assessments and conditional hearing costs are additional; this does not establish an active deployment. Statutory page carries a June 30, 2028 sunset.

sources.name: North Carolina General Assembly · G.S. 20-141
sources.notes: More than 15 mph over or over 80 mph is a Class 3 misdemeanor. A qualifying work-zone speeding violation adds $250 where required penalty signs are posted. Other charges and license action are separate.

sources.name: North Carolina General Assembly · G.S. 20-176
sources.notes: Unless a specific penalty otherwise applies, an Article infraction may carry a penalty not exceeding $100. This is a ceiling for the modeled infraction, not a fixed or payable fine.

sources.name: South Carolina Legislature · §56-5-1520(G)
sources.notes: First-offense ranges: 1–10 over $15–$25; more than 10 but less than 15 $25–$50; more than 15 but less than 25 $50–$75; more than 25 $75–$200 or possible imprisonment. The exact 15/25 boundaries are withheld because the published wording leaves interpretation/charge selection unresolved.

sources.name: South Carolina Legislature · §56-7-35
sources.notes: Traffic-stop, photographic-evidence and citation restrictions apply to speeding/signal tickets, with statutory exceptions. Toll and school-bus enforcement must not be represented as generic automated speeding-camera authority.

sources.name: Georgia Governor · Signed 2026 HB 651, §8
sources.notes: Signed act retains $75 first/$125 later school-zone camera penalties and initial 30-day warnings. §14 makes most provisions effective July 1, 2026; §§2 and 9 start July 1, 2027. Future referendum provisions are not applied to the November 2026 calculation. Processing charges are excluded.

sources.name: Georgia Governor · Signed 2026 HB 1161
sources.notes: Companion act changes school-zone device permitting and signs; ordinary provisions effective July 1, 2026, with §5 effective July 1, 2027. The calculation does not presume a permitted, operational school-zone installation or model all schedule/permit conditions.

sources.name: Florida Legislature · 2026 §318.18
sources.notes: Officer base schedule: 1–5 over warning, 6–9 $25, 10–14 $100, 15–19 $150, 20–29 $175. 30+ involves mandatory-hearing rules and is withheld. Posted school and qualifying staffed/signed construction zones have special amounts/doubling. School-camera fine is separately $100 under (3)(d).

sources.name: Florida Legislature · 2026 §316.1896
sources.notes: Local school-zone speed detection applies to more than 10 mph over in the specified school-session/breakfast/opening/closing windows. Warning-period and local authorization prerequisites apply; these conditions are not established by a map marker.

sources.name: Texas Legislature · Transportation §§542.401–542.404
sources.notes: General misdemeanor base fine where no other penalty is provided: $1–$200. Qualifying signed work zones with workers present and notation on the notice double minimum/maximum. Separate $3 and $50 state traffic fine provisions and court costs are excluded from the base comparison. The $50 provision includes a September 1, 2025 amendment.

sources.name: Texas Legislature · Transportation §542.2035
sources.notes: A municipality may not implement or operate the defined automated traffic control system on streets/highways under its jurisdiction to enforce posted speed limits. This is a scoped municipal restriction, not proof that there are no traffic, toll, plate-reader or officer-operated cameras.

sources.name: California Superior Court, Lassen · 2026 Uniform Bail and Penalty Schedule
sources.notes: 2026 ordinary speed-chart base amounts are $35 (1–15 over), $70 (16–25), $100 (26+). The court schedule shows much higher totals after assessments; no county-specific payable total is generalized statewide. Special zones, prior enhancements and speeds over 100 are excluded.

sources.name: DC Office of Documents · Adopted 18 DCMR §2600, R0056041
sources.notes: Downloaded the adopted rule file through its public View text action and checked the August 7, 2026 text: 1–10 over $50; 11–15 $100; 16–20 $150; 21–25 $200; 26+ controlled-access $400/other roads $500. This resolves the prior adopted-text hold.

sources.notes: Agency states automated-photo fines are the same as officer-issued speeding fines. School/work-zone moving fines double; those special-zone calculations remain withheld pending full conditions review.
